messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Minor Improvements to Figure
parts:
Dear All,
Please consider the code snippet at the end of the email.
There are a few points where I need some help.
(1) I still experience some problems when generating pdf files via Cairo.
Namely, if I uncomment the CairoPDF(...) line and remove the pdf(...),
the y-axis labeling is ugly (the '-' and the exponent merge no matter
what I try to do here). I am using the latest R 2.11 for an ubuntu
9.10 system. Any suggestions is appreciated (should I simply drop Cairo?).
(2) Axis ticking: I would like to have bigger ticks corresponding to the
exact powers of 10 (10,100,100; 1, 1e-1, 1e-2 etc...) along both the x
and y axis. Is that doable?
(3) Can I shift the ticks so that they are 'inside' the plot? See the
axis ticks in Fig. 2 in paper http://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4109
(4) Can I also have the same axis ticks along both the top horizontal
and right vertical axis (again, see the link above).
(5) Finally, can I make the axis titles, 'M(l)' and 'l' more tex-like,
i.e. more similar to $M(l)$ and $l$?

Many thanks

Lorenzo


library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)

ml_tmp <-
as.data.frame(cbind(seq(10,2e4,length=100),seq(1e-6,1,length=100) ))

names(ml_tmp) <- c("duration","p_contact")


mb <- c(seq(10,100, by=10),
seq(200,1e3,by=1e2),seq(2e3,1e4,by=1e3),seq(1e4,2e4,by=1e4))

my_sel <- seq(1,length(mb), by=9)

my_label2 <- rep("",length(mb))
my_label2[my_sel] <- expression(10^1 ,10^2,10^3,10^4)


mb3 <- c(seq(1e-6,1e-5, by=1e-6),
seq(2e-5,1e-4,by=1e-5),seq(2e-4,1e-3,by=1e-4),seq(2e-3,1e-2,by=1e-3),
seq(2e-2,1e-1,by=1e-2),seq(2e-1,1,by=1e-1))

my_sel <- seq(1,length(mb3), by=9)

my_label3 <- rep("",length(mb3))
my_label3[my_sel] <- expression(10^-6 ,10^-5,10^-4,10^-3,10^-2,10^-1,10^0)



gpl <- ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=duration, y=p_contact)) +
geom_point(size=6.5) +
opts( panel.background=theme_rect(fill='white'))+
xlab(expression(paste("l")))+
ylab(expression(paste("M(l)")))+
scale_x_continuous(trans="log10",
limits=c(10,2e4),breaks=mb,label=my_label2)+
scale_y_continuous(trans="log10", limits=c(1e-6,1),
breaks=mb3,label=my_label3)+
opts(plot.title = theme_text(size = 40))+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 40))+
opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 18, vjust=0.8))+
opts(legend.title = theme_text(size = 22,hjust=0))+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.ticks = theme_segment(colour = "black",
size=0.7),axis.ticks.length = unit(0.3, "cm"))+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+
opts(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.6),
legend.background=theme_rect(fill='white')
,legend.key = theme_rect(colour = NA))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 40, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=35, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=35, colour="black", hjust=1.1))


fn <- paste("test-plot.pdf")

pdf(fn)
#CairoPDF(fn)
print(gpl)
dev.off()



--

> y-axis labeling is ugly (the '-' and the exponent merge no matter what I try
> to do here). I  am using the latest R 2.11 for an ubuntu 9.10  system. Any
> suggestions is appreciated (should I simply drop Cairo?).
Have you tried the tikzDevice package?

> (2) Axis ticking: I would like to have bigger ticks corresponding to the
> exact powers of 10 (10,100,100; 1, 1e-1, 1e-2 etc...) along both the x and y
> axis. Is that doable?
> (3) Can I shift the ticks so that they are 'inside' the plot? See the axis
> ticks in Fig. 2 in paper http://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4109

I think you could drop the default tick marks altogether and replace
them with a call to geom_segment(). This way the ticks will be inside
the plot region, and you can set the width that you want for each of
them. The major drawback is that you'll have to define the tick
positions manually.

> (4)  Can  I also have  the same axis ticks along both the top horizontal and
> right vertical axis (again, see the link above).

You could set the exact limits for both axes using expand=c(0,0) in
scale_x(y)_continuous().

> (5) Finally, can I make the axis titles, 'M(l)' and 'l' more tex-like, i.e.
> more similar to $M(l)$ and $l$?
>

Again, tikzDevice can help you here.

HTH,

baptiste

On Sun, Apr 25, 2010 at 5:21 PM, hadley wickham <h.wi...@gmail.com> wrote:

>
> No, the major drawback is that you'll have ticks inside your plot ;)

I trust (and agree with) your judgment, but would you have a reference
on this? People are pretty conservative in my field of research when
it comes to graphics (and more) -- they demand white background, big
and small tick marks (often inside), a heavy surrounding box, and axes
that meet at the edges (no expand), not to mention the Matlab color
palette and other fantastic absurdities...

I have to say, I kind of miss the distinction primary / secondary tick
marks in R.

Best,

baptiste

messages.subject: stat_summary syntax
parts:
I am having a problem with stat_summary syntax.

I am able to get the graph I want with the qplot syntax (see below), but
not able to get the same graph with the ggplot syntax.

The qplot statement plots two points (as desired), but the ggplot
command plots two vertical lines (from min to max with strata) and the
graph does not plot the mean, as I had hoped.

What is wrong with the syntax of the ggplot statement?


example<-data.frame(
data=c(rnorm(1000,mean=0.01,sd=.002)),
site=c(replicate(500,'A'), replicate(500,'B'))
)

qplot(data=example, x=site, y=data, stat="summary", fun.y = 'mean')

ggplot(data=example)+geom_line(aes(x=site, y=data))+stat_summary(fun.y=mean)

messages.subject: Re: stat_summary syntax
parts:
I believe that the aesthetic you want is outside the scope of
stat_summary the way you have it defined. Try something along the lines of

ggplot(data=example) + aes(x=site, y=data) +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean,color="red",fun.ymin=mean,fun.ymax=mean)

or

ggplot(data=example, aes(x=site,y=data)) +
geom_point() +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean,color="red",fun.ymin=min,fun.ymax=max)
